description: Replace the current minimal project view with a comprehensive branch management view for multi-repo projects. The view should show all branches per repo with change indicators (dirty, ahead/behind), allow checkout/creation of branches, and support creating merge requests via glab/gh CLI.

title: Hunk-level staging in CommitView
description:
In the staging view, show file diffs with hunk boundaries and allow staging/unstaging individual hunks.

## Requirements
- Enter on a file in CommitView opens diff preview with hunk boundaries
- Each hunk visually distinct and selectable
- Space on a hunk stages/unstages just that hunk
- Use git apply --cached with constructed patch for staging, --reverse for unstaging
- Diff refreshes after each hunk operation

## New types and functions in internal/git/diff.go
- DiffHunk struct: Header, Lines []DiffLine, OldStart, OldCount, NewStart, NewCount
- ParseHunks(rawDiff string) []DiffHunk
- StageHunk(repoPath, filePath string, hunk DiffHunk) error
- UnstageHunk(repoPath, filePath string, hunk DiffHunk) error

## Files to modify
- internal/git/diff.go - DiffHunk struct, ParseHunks, StageHunk, UnstageHunk
- internal/app/views/commit.go - diff preview mode with hunk nav and staging

## Patterns to follow
- DiffView.parseDiff() for parsing
- DiffView.renderDiffWithGutter() for rendering
- CommitView.stageFile()/unstageFile() for execution pattern
- git apply --cached: construct patch with file header + single hunk

## Acceptance criteria
- Enter on file shows diff with hunk boundaries
- Each hunk selectable, Space stages/unstages individual hunks
- Diff refreshes after hunk operations
- Works for both staged and unstaged sections
- Esc returns to file list

title: Line-level staging in CommitView

- Individual + and - lines can be toggled
- 'v' starts visual/range selection, j/k extends it

- UnstageLines(repoPath, filePath string, hunk DiffHunk, selectedLineIndices []int) error

## Acceptance criteria
- 'l' enters line-selection mode
- Individual +/- lines toggleable
- 'v' starts visual range selection

title: Project View Rework: Multi-Repo Feature Workflow with Worktrees & Agent Orchestration
description:
## Overview

Rework the Project View (multi-repo mode) from a read-only branch browser into a full feature development workflow. The current Project View shows repos with expandable branches and supports basic checkout/MR creation per-repo. This epic transforms it into an orchestrated multi-repo feature workflow where users can:

1. **Create worktrees** across all repos in a project for a feature branch (one worktree per repo, all on the same branch name)
2. **Spawn Claude Code agents** into those worktrees to implement features across the codebase
3. **Monitor agent progress** across all repos from a unified dashboard
4. **Push all repos** that have changes on the feature branch in a batch operation
5. **Batch-create MRs/PRs** across all repos for the feature branch
6. **Cleanup** by removing worktrees across all repos when the feature is done

## Motivation

Multi-repo development (microservices, monorepo-adjacent patterns) requires coordinating the same feature branch across many repositories. Currently, users must manually create branches/worktrees, start agents, push, and create MRs for each repo individually. This epic provides a streamlined "feature workflow" that automates these repetitive cross-repo operations.

## User Flow

1. User opens project mode (`--project-config` or `--repo` pointing at parent directory)
2. From Project View, user presses `w` to start a new feature workflow
3. User enters a branch name (e.g., `feature/add-auth`)
4. System creates worktrees in all repos for that branch (under a configurable base directory, e.g., `~/.worktrees/<project>/<branch>/<repo>`)
5. User can then press `a` to spawn agents into the worktrees with a shared prompt
6. Dashboard shows agent status per repo (running/done/error)
7. When work is complete, user presses `p` to push all repos with changes
8. User presses `M` to batch-create MRs/PRs across all repos
9. User presses `D` to cleanup: remove all worktrees for the feature branch

## Architecture

The feature builds on existing primitives:
- `project.Project` for multi-repo management
- `git.CreateWorktree/RemoveWorktree` for worktree operations
- `engine.Engine` for agent subprocess management
- `git.Push/SetUpstreamAndPush` for push operations
- `git.CreateMergeRequestCLI` for MR/PR creation

New concept: **FeatureWorkflow** - a stateful object that tracks the lifecycle of a cross-repo feature branch including worktree paths, agent IDs, push status, and MR URLs per repo.

title: Add FeatureWorkflow model and project-level worktree orchestration
description:
## Context

The git-frontend TUI application supports multi-repo projects via the project package (internal/project/). A Project contains multiple Repos, each with a Path, Name, and DefaultBranch. The project can refresh all repos concurrently and aggregate their status.

Currently, there is no concept of a coordinated "feature workflow" that spans multiple repos. When a user wants to work on a feature across all repos in a project, they must manually create worktrees/branches in each repo one at a time. This task introduces a FeatureWorkflow model that tracks the lifecycle of a cross-repo feature branch: which worktrees were created, their paths, and the overall state of the workflow.

The git package already has worktree primitives: CreateWorktree, RemoveWorktree, GetWorktrees, PruneWorktrees (in internal/git/stash.go lines 216-282). The branch creation primitive is CreateBranch (internal/git/branch.go line 72). This task orchestrates these primitives across all repos in a project.

## Requirements

### FeatureWorkflow struct
- Lives in internal/project/workflow.go (NEW file)
- Fields:
  - BranchName string - the feature branch name (e.g., "feature/add-auth")
  - BaseDir string - the base directory where worktrees are created (e.g., ~/.worktrees/<project>/<branch>/)
  - Repos map[string]*WorkflowRepo - keyed by repo name
  - State WorkflowState - enum: Initializing, Active, PushingAll, CreatingMRs, CleaningUp, Done
  - CreatedAt time.Time
  - Error string

### WorkflowRepo struct
- RepoName string
- OriginalPath string - the main repo path
- WorktreePath string - the worktree path for this repo
- WorktreeCreated bool
- AgentID string - agent session ID if an agent was spawned
- Pushed bool
- MRURL string - URL of created MR/PR
- Error string

### WorkflowState enum
- WorkflowInitializing, WorkflowActive, WorkflowPushingAll, WorkflowCreatingMRs, WorkflowCleaningUp, WorkflowDone

### Functions to implement

1. NewFeatureWorkflow(proj *Project, branchName string, baseDir string) *FeatureWorkflow
   - Initializes the workflow with one WorkflowRepo per project repo
   - Computes worktree paths: baseDir/<repoName> (e.g., ~/.worktrees/myproject/feature-add-auth/api-service/)
   - Sets state to WorkflowInitializing

2. (fw *FeatureWorkflow) CreateAllWorktrees() error
   - Iterates all repos concurrently (use sync.WaitGroup like Project.Refresh does)
   - For each repo, calls git.CreateWorktree(repo.OriginalPath, worktreePath, branchName, true)
   - The createBranch=true flag creates a new branch if it doesn't exist
   - Records success/failure per repo in WorkflowRepo.Error
   - Sets state to WorkflowActive when done
   - Returns error only for total failure; partial failures are recorded per-repo

3. (fw *FeatureWorkflow) RemoveAllWorktrees() error
   - Iterates all repos concurrently
   - For each repo where WorktreeCreated is true, calls git.RemoveWorktree(repo.OriginalPath, worktreePath, true)
   - Sets state to WorkflowDone when complete

4. (fw *FeatureWorkflow) PushAll() error
   - Iterates all repos concurrently
   - For each repo where WorktreeCreated is true:
     - Check if the worktree has changes to push using git.GetUpstreamStatus(worktreePath)
     - If ahead > 0 or no upstream, call git.SetUpstreamAndPush(worktreePath, "origin")
     - Record success/failure per repo

5. (fw *FeatureWorkflow) CreateAllMRs() error
   - Iterates repos sequentially (to avoid rate limits)
   - For each repo where Pushed is true:
     - Detect provider with git.DetectRemoteProvider(repo.OriginalPath)
     - Call git.CreateMergeRequestCLI(repo.WorktreePath, provider)
     - Store result URL in WorkflowRepo.MRURL

6. (fw *FeatureWorkflow) Status() *WorkflowStatus
   - Returns a summary: how many worktrees created, how many agents running, how many pushed, how many MRs created, errors

### Thread safety
- Use sync.RWMutex for the workflow struct (same pattern as project.Project)
- Individual WorkflowRepo fields are only written by one goroutine at a time (during concurrent ops, each goroutine owns its repo)

## Architecture & Data Flow

The FeatureWorkflow sits between the Project (which knows about repos) and the git package (which does the actual git operations). It is a stateful orchestrator:

```
ProjectView (UI) → FeatureWorkflow → git.CreateWorktree / git.Push / git.CreateMergeRequestCLI
                                    → engine.Engine.StartAgent (for spawning agents)
```

The workflow does NOT own the engine -- agent spawning will be handled by the UI layer passing agent IDs back to the workflow. The workflow just tracks which agent ID is associated with which repo.

## Technical Constraints & Patterns
- Follow the concurrency pattern from Project.Refresh() in internal/project/project.go lines 111-124 (sync.WaitGroup + goroutines per repo)
- Follow the error-per-repo pattern from Project.BranchExistsAcross() in internal/project/project.go lines 152-177
- Use the existing git functions, do NOT duplicate their logic
- The baseDir should sanitize branch names for filesystem use (replace / with -)

## Reference Files
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/project/project.go - Project struct, Refresh() concurrency pattern, Repo struct
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/git/stash.go lines 216-282 - CreateWorktree, RemoveWorktree functions
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/git/sync.go - Push, SetUpstreamAndPush, GetUpstreamStatus functions
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/git/remote.go - DetectRemoteProvider, CreateMergeRequestCLI functions
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/git/branch.go - CreateBranch function

## Files to Create/Modify
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/project/workflow.go (NEW) - FeatureWorkflow struct, WorkflowRepo struct, WorkflowState enum, all orchestration functions
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/project/workflow_test.go (NEW) - Unit tests for workflow creation, status aggregation, branch name sanitization

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] FeatureWorkflow struct exists with BranchName, BaseDir, Repos map, State, CreatedAt
- [ ] WorkflowRepo tracks worktree path, creation status, agent ID, push status, MR URL, error
- [ ] NewFeatureWorkflow correctly computes worktree paths from project repos
- [ ] CreateAllWorktrees creates worktrees concurrently across all repos, records per-repo success/failure
- [ ] RemoveAllWorktrees removes worktrees concurrently, handles missing worktrees gracefully
- [ ] PushAll pushes repos with changes, skips repos without changes, records per-repo status
- [ ] CreateAllMRs creates MRs sequentially, stores URLs, handles errors per-repo
- [ ] Status() returns accurate counts of created worktrees, agents, pushes, MRs
- [ ] Branch names with slashes are sanitized for filesystem paths (feature/add-auth becomes feature-add-auth)
- [ ] Thread-safe access to workflow state via RWMutex
- [ ] Unit tests cover workflow creation and status aggregation

title: Add feature workflow UI to ProjectView: worktree creation and cleanup
description:
## Context

The git-frontend TUI has a ProjectView (internal/app/views/project.go) that displays multi-repo project status as an expandable tree of repos and branches. Users can navigate with j/k, expand/collapse repos with Enter, checkout branches with c, create branches across repos with n, and create MRs with m. The view uses a components.Filter[treeNode] for the scrollable list.

This task adds the first phase of the feature workflow UI: the ability to start a new feature workflow (which creates worktrees across all repos), see the active workflow status, and cleanup worktrees when done. This builds on the FeatureWorkflow model from internal/project/workflow.go.

The ProjectView currently has modal states for branch check (showBranchCheck), new branch creation (showNewBranch), and MR confirmation (showMRConfirm). The workflow UI follows the same modal pattern.

## Requirements

### New state fields on ProjectView
- activeWorkflow *project.FeatureWorkflow - the currently active feature workflow (nil when no workflow active)
- showWorkflowStart bool - modal for entering branch name to start workflow
- workflowBranchName string - input text for branch name
- showWorkflowCleanup bool - confirmation modal for cleanup
- workflowStatusMsg string - flash message for workflow operations
- workflowBaseDir string - computed from project config or default (~/.worktrees/<projectName>/)

### New keybindings (added to main view, not in modal state)
- `w` - Start new feature workflow: opens branch name input modal
- `D` - Cleanup feature workflow: shows confirmation, then removes all worktrees
- `W` - Show/hide workflow status panel (toggle)

### Workflow start modal (showWorkflowStart)
- Renders similar to showNewBranch modal: header + text input + Enter/Esc hint
- Title: "Start Feature Workflow (create worktrees across all repos)"
- Input: branch name (e.g., feature/add-auth)
- On Enter: creates FeatureWorkflow and calls CreateAllWorktrees()
- Show per-repo results (checkmark/x + repo name) as a flash message
- On Esc: cancel

### Workflow cleanup confirmation (showWorkflowCleanup)
- Only available when activeWorkflow is not nil
- Renders similar to showMRConfirm: "Remove all worktrees for <branch>? (y/n)"
- On y: calls activeWorkflow.RemoveAllWorktrees(), sets activeWorkflow to nil
- Show per-repo results as flash message

### Workflow status panel
- When activeWorkflow is not nil and W is pressed, show a status summary above the repo tree
- Show: branch name, state, per-repo status (worktree created, agent running, pushed, MR URL)
- Compact format: one line per repo with status icons

### Updated help bar
- Add w, D, W keybindings to the footer help text
- Add to KeyBindings() return list

### CapturesInput / CapturesKey updates
- CapturesInput returns true when showWorkflowStart or showWorkflowCleanup is true
- CapturesKey adds "w", "W", "D" to the list

## Architecture & Data Flow

```
User presses 'w' → showWorkflowStart = true → user types branch name → Enter
→ project.NewFeatureWorkflow(proj, branchName, baseDir) 
→ workflow.CreateAllWorktrees() (runs as async tea.Cmd)
→ On completion: set activeWorkflow, show results flash
```

The worktree creation is a potentially slow operation (creates git worktrees for each repo). It should run as an async tea.Cmd (return a func() tea.Msg from Update) so the UI doesn't freeze. Follow the pattern used by Init() and the 'r' refresh key in the existing ProjectView.

## Technical Constraints & Patterns
- Follow the existing modal pattern in ProjectView.Update() - showBranchCheck/showNewBranch/showMRConfirm handlers (internal/app/views/project.go lines 332-400)
- Follow the text input pattern: KeyBackspace, KeyEnter, KeyEsc, KeyRunes (same file, lines 334-361)
- Run slow operations as async tea.Cmd returning RefreshDoneMsg (same file, lines 412-417)
- The baseDir default should be computed as: ~/.worktrees/<sanitized-project-name>/
- Use ctrl+w for word deletion in text inputs (same pattern as worktree.go line 277)

## Reference Files
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/project.go - Existing ProjectView with all modal patterns, key handling, rendering
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/project/workflow.go - FeatureWorkflow model (from task git-frontend-14)
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/worktree.go - WorktreeView for UI pattern reference

## Integration Points
- **Depends on**: project.FeatureWorkflow (git-frontend-14)
- **Used by**: Agent orchestration task (will read activeWorkflow to know where to spawn agents)
- **Shares state with**: The tree view - when a workflow is active, the tree should visually indicate which repos have worktrees

## Files to Create/Modify
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/project.go (UPDATE) - Add workflow state fields, keybindings, modal handlers, rendering, CapturesInput/CapturesKey updates

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Pressing 'w' opens a branch name input modal
- [ ] Entering a branch name and pressing Enter creates worktrees across all repos
- [ ] Per-repo results (success/failure) shown as flash message after worktree creation
- [ ] activeWorkflow is set and tracks the current feature workflow state
- [ ] Pressing 'D' when workflow is active shows cleanup confirmation
- [ ] Confirming cleanup removes all worktrees and clears the active workflow
- [ ] Pressing 'W' toggles a workflow status panel showing per-repo status
- [ ] Help bar and KeyBindings() updated with new keys
- [ ] CapturesInput returns true during modal states
- [ ] Slow operations (worktree create/remove) run as async tea.Cmd, not blocking UI
- [ ] Esc cancels all modal states
- [ ] ctrl+w deletes word in text input

title: Add agent orchestration to feature workflow: spawn agents into worktrees
description:
## Context

The git-frontend TUI has an agent engine (internal/engine/engine.go) that manages Claude Code subprocesses. Agents are started with engine.StartAgent(projectPath, task, opts) which takes a working directory, a task string, and options including context files, model selection, and smart routing. The engine supports concurrent agents with configurable limits (default 10).

The ProjectView (internal/app/views/project.go) is being extended with a FeatureWorkflow that creates worktrees across all repos for a feature branch. This task adds the ability to spawn agents into those worktrees, letting users describe a task and have Claude Code work on it in parallel across all repos.

The existing AgentView (internal/app/views/agent.go) shows agents in a list with live streaming output. This task does NOT modify the AgentView -- instead, it adds agent spawning controls to the ProjectView and records agent IDs in the workflow so users can later switch to the Agents view (F5) to monitor them.

## Requirements

### New state fields on ProjectView
- engine *engine.Engine - reference to the agent engine (passed during construction or via setter)
- showAgentPrompt bool - modal for entering agent task prompt
- agentPromptText string - the task text input
- agentSpawnResults string - flash message showing which repos got agents

### New keybinding
- `a` - Spawn agents into worktrees: only available when activeWorkflow is not nil and worktrees are created
  - Opens a text input modal for the agent task prompt
  - On Enter: spawns an agent into each repo's worktree directory
  - On Esc: cancel

### Agent spawning logic
When the user enters a prompt and presses Enter:
1. For each repo in the active workflow where WorktreeCreated is true:
   - Call engine.StartAgent(repo.WorktreePath, promptText, opts)
   - opts should include:
     - ContextFiles from the project (proj.ContextFiles)
     - SmartRoute: true (to use the Haiku classifier for model selection)
   - Store the returned agent ID in WorkflowRepo.AgentID
2. Record results per-repo in agentSpawnResults flash message
3. The agents work independently in their worktrees -- no coordination needed between them

### Agent status in workflow panel
- When showing the workflow status panel (toggle 'W'), include agent status per repo:
  - No agent: show "-"
  - Agent running: show "● running" with elapsed time
  - Agent complete: show "✓ done"
  - Agent error: show "✗ error"
- To get agent state, query engine.GetStatus(agentID) for each WorkflowRepo.AgentID

### Updated CapturesInput / CapturesKey
- CapturesInput returns true when showAgentPrompt is true
- CapturesKey adds "a" to the list

### Constructor change
- NewProjectView and NewProjectViewWithPath need to accept an optional *engine.Engine parameter
- Or add a SetEngine(*engine.Engine) setter method (preferred, matches AgentView pattern at internal/app/views/agent.go line 124)
- Also need to accept optional context files ([]string) or get them from the project

### Text input for prompt
- The prompt should support multi-word input (not just branch name)
- Follow the same text input pattern: runes, backspace, ctrl+w, Enter, Esc
- Display the prompt in a box similar to the AgentView new-agent input (internal/app/views/agent.go lines 785-812)

## Architecture & Data Flow

```
User presses 'a' → showAgentPrompt = true → user types task → Enter
→ For each WorkflowRepo where WorktreeCreated:
    engine.StartAgent(worktreePath, task, AgentOptions{ContextFiles, SmartRoute})
    → store agent ID in WorkflowRepo.AgentID
→ Show flash message with results
→ User switches to Agents view (F5) to monitor progress
```

The agents run as background subprocesses managed by the engine. They stream JSON output that the AgentView renders. The ProjectView only needs to track agent IDs and query their status for the workflow panel.

## Technical Constraints & Patterns
- Follow the new-agent input pattern from AgentView.handleNewAgentInput() in internal/app/views/agent.go lines 526-558
- Follow the engine.StartAgent call pattern from AgentView (same file, lines 529-537)
- Agent options should include SmartRoute: true and ContextFiles from the project
- Do NOT run agent spawning as a blocking call in the Update handler -- each StartAgent call starts a background process and returns immediately, so sequential spawning in a loop is fine (unlike worktree creation which does actual disk I/O)
- The engine has a max agents limit -- if spawning would exceed it, show an error

## Reference Files
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/engine/engine.go - Engine.StartAgent, AgentOptions, capacity checking
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/engine/agent.go - Agent struct, AgentState enum, Snapshot()
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/agent.go lines 526-558 - New agent input handling pattern
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/agent.go lines 78-99 - NewAgentView constructor with engine and context files
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/project.go - ProjectView to modify
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/project/workflow.go - FeatureWorkflow (from git-frontend-14)

## Integration Points
- **Depends on**: FeatureWorkflow model (git-frontend-14), Workflow UI (git-frontend-15)
- **Uses**: engine.Engine for agent management
- **Used by**: Workflow status panel (reads agent states)
- **Related**: AgentView (F5) shows the same agents that this spawns; they share the engine instance

## Files to Create/Modify
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/project.go (UPDATE) - Add engine field, SetEngine method, agent prompt modal, agent spawning logic, agent status in workflow panel
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/app.go (UPDATE) - Pass engine to ProjectView in initProjectRouter() (line 272), similar to how AgentView gets the engine (lines 187-194)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ProjectView has a SetEngine method and stores an *engine.Engine reference
- [ ] Pressing 'a' when a workflow is active opens a task prompt modal
- [ ] Entering a task and pressing Enter spawns agents into all worktrees with created worktrees
- [ ] Agent IDs are stored in WorkflowRepo.AgentID
- [ ] Context files from the project are passed to agent options
- [ ] Smart routing is enabled for agent spawning
- [ ] Flash message shows per-repo spawn results (success/failure + agent ID)
- [ ] Workflow status panel shows agent state per repo (-, running, done, error)
- [ ] Engine capacity is checked before spawning; error shown if limit exceeded
- [ ] Esc cancels the prompt modal
- [ ] ctrl+w deletes word in prompt input
- [ ] Engine is wired to ProjectView in app.go initProjectRouter()

title: Add batch push and batch MR creation to feature workflow UI
description:
## Context

The git-frontend TUI's ProjectView (internal/app/views/project.go) is being extended with a FeatureWorkflow that manages cross-repo feature development. Previous tasks added the FeatureWorkflow model with PushAll() and CreateAllMRs() methods (internal/project/workflow.go), worktree creation/cleanup UI, and agent spawning.

This task adds the batch push and batch MR creation UI to the ProjectView, completing the feature development lifecycle: create worktrees → spawn agents → push all → create MRs → cleanup.

The git package already has push functions: git.Push(repoPath, force) and git.SetUpstreamAndPush(repoPath, remote) in internal/git/sync.go. MR creation is handled by git.CreateMergeRequestCLI(repoPath, provider) in internal/git/remote.go and git.DetectRemoteProvider(repoPath) for forge detection.

## Requirements

### New keybindings (when activeWorkflow is not nil)
- `p` (lowercase) - Batch push: push all repos in the workflow that have unpushed changes
  - Shows a confirmation modal: "Push all repos on branch <branch>? (y/n)"
  - On y: runs workflow.PushAll() as an async tea.Cmd
  - Shows per-repo results as flash message (pushed, skipped, error)
- `M` (capital) - Batch create MRs: create MRs/PRs across all repos
  - Only available after pushing (at least one repo has Pushed=true)
  - Shows a confirmation modal: "Create MRs for all pushed repos? (y/n)"
  - On y: runs workflow.CreateAllMRs() as async tea.Cmd
  - Shows per-repo results as flash message (MR URL or error)

### New state fields on ProjectView
- showPushConfirm bool - confirmation for batch push
- showBatchMRConfirm bool - confirmation for batch MR creation
- pushResults string - flash message with push results
- mrResults string - flash message with MR results

### Confirmation modal rendering
- Follow the existing showMRConfirm pattern (internal/app/views/project.go lines 601-612)
- Push confirm: "Push all repos on branch '<branchName>'? [y] Yes [n] No"
- MR confirm: "Create MRs/PRs for <N> pushed repos? [y] Yes [n] No"

### Push results display
- Per-repo line: "✓ repo-name: pushed (↑N commits)" or "⊘ repo-name: nothing to push" or "✗ repo-name: error message"
- Show as flash message (same pattern as newBranchResult)

### MR results display
- Per-repo line: "✓ repo-name: <MR URL>" or "✗ repo-name: error message" or "⊘ repo-name: skipped (not pushed)"
- Show as flash message

### Workflow status panel updates
- After push: show push status per repo (pushed/not pushed)
- After MR creation: show MR URLs per repo

### Updated CapturesInput / CapturesKey
- CapturesInput returns true when showPushConfirm or showBatchMRConfirm is true
- CapturesKey: note that lowercase 'p' conflicts with the prune worktree key in the existing worktree view, but in project view it's currently unused. If there's a conflict with an existing key, use 'P' instead.

### Error handling
- If no workflow is active and user presses p/M, show flash message "No active workflow"
- If push is attempted but no worktrees have changes, show "Nothing to push - all repos are up to date"
- If MR creation is attempted but no repos are pushed, show "No repos have been pushed yet"

## Architecture & Data Flow

```
User presses 'p' → showPushConfirm = true → 'y'
→ async: workflow.PushAll() [runs git push in each worktree concurrently]
→ On completion: show results flash, update workflow status

User presses 'M' → showBatchMRConfirm = true → 'y'
→ async: workflow.CreateAllMRs() [runs MR creation sequentially to avoid rate limits]
→ On completion: show results flash with MR URLs, update workflow status
```

Both push and MR creation are potentially slow operations. They MUST run as async tea.Cmd (return func() tea.Msg from Update) so the TUI remains responsive. Follow the same pattern as the worktree creation async operation.

## Technical Constraints & Patterns
- Follow the confirmation modal pattern from showMRConfirm (internal/app/views/project.go lines 385-399)

- Flash messages should clear on next key press (same as newBranchResult/mrResult pattern, lines 325-329)
- The workflow.PushAll() method handles the per-repo push logic; the UI just calls it and displays results
- The workflow.CreateAllMRs() method handles MR creation; the UI calls it and displays results with URLs

title: Wire ProjectView workflow features into project router and add Agents view
description:
## Context

The git-frontend TUI supports two modes: single-repo mode (with a full set of views: Overview, Branches, Commit, Log, Agents, plus git submenu) and project mode (currently only has a single Project view accessible via F1). The router is set up in internal/app/app.go: initRouter() for single-repo mode (lines 167-234) and initProjectRouter() for project mode (lines 238-284).

In project mode, the router currently only registers a single "Project" view:

```go
projectView := views.NewProjectView(m.proj)
router := NewRouter(projectView, "Project")
router.viewKeys["Project"] = "f1"
router.keyToView["f1"] = "Project"
```

The feature workflow (previous tasks) adds worktree creation, agent spawning, batch push, and MR creation to the ProjectView. However, agents spawned from the Project view need to be monitorable -- currently, there is no Agents view registered in project mode. Users need to be able to switch to the Agents view (F5) to monitor agent output with the full split-pane agent console.

Additionally, when a user presses 'o' on a repo in the ProjectView, it currently does a ViewChangeMsg that switches the entire app to single-repo mode. With the workflow active, users should instead get a per-repo view within project mode -- or at minimum, the agent view should be available alongside the project view.

This task wires up the project router to include the Agents view and ensures the engine, context files, and project references are properly connected.

## Requirements

### Register Agents view in project mode
- In initProjectRouter(), after creating the Project view, also create and register an AgentView
- Pass the engine and project context files to the AgentView
- Register it with F5 shortcut (matching single-repo mode)
- This allows Tab/F5 to switch between Project (F1) and Agents (F5)

### Pass engine to ProjectView
- In initProjectRouter(), create the engine if it doesn't exist (same as initRouter line 188)
- Call projectView.SetEngine(m.engine) after creating the ProjectView
- Pass project.ContextFiles to the ProjectView as well

### Handle ViewChangeMsg from ProjectView
- Currently when 'o' is pressed in ProjectView, it emits ViewChangeMsg{ViewName: "Overview", RepoPath: node.Repo.Path}
- The app.go Update handler (line 475-487) switches to single-repo mode when RepoPath is set
- This is fine for browsing individual repos, but when a workflow is active, the user should be warned or the workflow state should be preserved
- For now: preserve existing behavior (drilling into single-repo mode resets project mode) but add a flash message if a workflow is active: "Warning: leaving project mode will disconnect from active workflow"

### Project-mode tab bar
- With two views (Project, Agents), the tab bar should show both
- Verify that Tab cycling works between Project and Agents
- Verify that F1 returns to Project, F5 goes to Agents

### Agent spawning from ProjectView uses the shared engine
- The ProjectView spawns agents via its engine reference
- The AgentView sees the same agents because it shares the same engine instance
- No additional wiring needed beyond passing the same *engine.Engine to both

### Git submenu for project mode (optional but recommended)
- Consider registering a subset of the git submenu views for project mode
- At minimum: Sync and Pipeline views could be useful when drilling into a repo
- This is optional for this task -- can be deferred

## Architecture & Data Flow

```
app.go initProjectRouter():
  1. Create engine (or reuse existing)
  2. Create ProjectView with project reference
  3. Call projectView.SetEngine(engine)
  4. Create AgentView with repo path and engine and context files
  5. Register both in router: Project (F1), Agents (F5)

User flow:
  Project (F1) → spawn agents via 'a' → agents appear in engine
  → Tab or F5 → Agents view → see all agents with streaming output
  → Tab or F1 → back to Project view → see workflow status
```

## Technical Constraints & Patterns
- Follow the initRouter() pattern in internal/app/app.go lines 167-234 for view registration
- Follow the engine initialization pattern at lines 187-188
- Follow the AgentView construction pattern at lines 190-195
- The repoPath for the AgentView in project mode should be the project directory (first repo's path or the project base dir)
- Context files come from m.proj.ContextFiles

## Reference Files
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/app.go lines 238-284 - Current initProjectRouter() to modify
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/app.go lines 167-234 - initRouter() as pattern for full view registration
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/agent.go lines 78-99 - NewAgentView constructor
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/project.go - ProjectView with SetEngine method (from git-frontend-16)
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/router.go - Router.Register, RegisterSubmenu, Tab cycling

## Integration Points
- **Depends on**: ProjectView workflow features (git-frontend-15, git-frontend-16)
- **Connects**: ProjectView (agent spawning) ↔ AgentView (agent monitoring) via shared engine
- **Modifies**: App initialization for project mode

## Files to Create/Modify
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/app.go (UPDATE) - Expand initProjectRouter() to register Agents view, create/pass engine, pass context files to ProjectView

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] initProjectRouter() creates an engine and passes it to both ProjectView and AgentView
- [ ] Agents view is registered in project mode with F5 shortcut
- [ ] Tab cycling works between Project (F1) and Agents (F5) in project mode
- [ ] Agents spawned from ProjectView's workflow appear in the Agents view
- [ ] Agent output is streamable from the Agents view in project mode
- [ ] Context files from the project are passed to both AgentView and ProjectView
- [ ] Tab bar shows both Project and Agents tabs
- [ ] Flash message warns user when leaving project mode with active workflow (pressing 'o' to drill into repo)

title: Add workflow status indicators to project tree and unified status panel
description:
## Context

The git-frontend TUI's ProjectView (internal/app/views/project.go) renders a tree of repos and branches using a components.Filter[treeNode]. Each repo row shows: expand indicator (triangle), status icon (checkmark/dot/x), repo name, current branch, branch count, and ahead count. Each branch row shows: indentation, current branch marker, branch name, and ahead/behind indicators.

Previous tasks added a FeatureWorkflow to the ProjectView that tracks worktrees, agents, push status, and MR URLs per repo. This task enhances the tree rendering and adds a comprehensive status panel to make the workflow state visible at a glance without needing to toggle a separate panel.

## Requirements

### Tree rendering enhancements (inline workflow indicators)

When a FeatureWorkflow is active, enhance the repo rows in renderTreeNode() to show workflow status inline:

1. **Worktree indicator**: When a repo has a worktree created for the workflow, show a "🌿" (or "W") icon after the repo name
2. **Agent indicator**: When a repo has an active agent:
   - Running: show "◐" spinning icon (or cycle through ◐◓◑◒ on each tick)
   - Complete: show "✓"
   - Error: show "✗"
   After the worktree indicator
3. **Push indicator**: When a repo has been pushed, show "↑" after the agent indicator
4. **MR indicator**: When a repo has an MR created, show "⎆" (or "MR") with a link indicator

Example repo row with workflow active:
```
  ▼ ✓ api-service  feature/add-auth  (5 branches)  🌿 ✓ ↑ ⎆
```

### Unified workflow status panel

The workflow status panel (toggled with 'W', from git-frontend-15) should render as a compact section above the repo tree with the following layout:

```
╭ Feature Workflow: feature/add-auth ─────────────────────────╮
│ State: Active  │  Worktrees: 3/3  │  Agents: 1● 2✓  │  Pushed: 2/3  │  MRs: 0/3  │
│                                                                                      │
│  api-service      🌿✓  ● running 45s                                                │
│  web-frontend     🌿✓  ✓ done ($0.12)     ↑pushed    ⎆ https://...                 │
│  shared-lib       🌿✓  ✗ error            -          -                               │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Panel sections:
1. **Header**: Branch name and workflow state
2. **Summary bar**: Aggregate counts (worktrees created/total, agents by state, pushed/total, MRs/total)
3. **Per-repo detail**: One line per repo with worktree, agent, push, MR status

For agent status details:
- Query engine.GetAgent(agentID) to get the Agent, then agent.Snapshot() for state
- Show elapsed time for running agents (time.Since(startedAt))
- Show cost for completed agents (TotalCostUSD)

### Auto-refresh for live agent status
- The ProjectView currently refreshes via manual 'r' press
- When a workflow is active with running agents, add a periodic refresh (StreamTickMsg pattern from AgentView)
- Use a 1-second tick interval when agents are running
- Stop the tick when no agents are running
- The tick should only refresh the workflow panel, not the full repo tree (to avoid expensive git operations)

### Rendering adjustments
- The workflow panel should be rendered above the repo tree in the View() method
- When the panel is visible, reduce the filter height to accommodate the panel
- Panel height: 3 (header + summary) + N (per-repo lines) + 2 (borders)

## Architecture & Data Flow

```
StreamTickMsg (1s interval) → loadWorkflowStatus()
  → For each WorkflowRepo with AgentID:
      engine.GetAgent(agentID).Snapshot() → get state, elapsed, cost
  → Update display strings
  → No full repo refresh (just workflow status)
```

## Technical Constraints & Patterns
- Follow the renderTreeNode() pattern in internal/app/views/project.go lines 215-318 for adding inline indicators
- Follow the StreamTickMsg pattern from AgentView (internal/app/views/agent.go lines 141-145, 500-502) for periodic refresh
- Use theme styles consistently (th.DashboardAccentStyle for positive, th.DashboardErrorStyle for errors, th.MutedTextStyle for inactive)
- The status panel should use box-drawing characters (lipgloss border or manual ╭╮╰╯│─) for visual separation
- Keep the panel compact -- it should not overwhelm the repo tree

## Reference Files
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/project.go lines 215-318 - renderTreeNode() to enhance with workflow indicators
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/project.go lines 500-657 - View() to add workflow panel
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/agent.go lines 141-145 - StreamTickMsg pattern for periodic refresh
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/agent.go lines 594-668 - renderAgentItem() for agent state icon/style reference
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/engine/agent.go lines 572-603 - Agent.Snapshot() for reading agent state
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/theme/theme.go - Theme styles for consistent colors

## Integration Points
- **Depends on**: All previous workflow tasks (git-frontend-14 through git-frontend-18)
- **Reads from**: engine.Engine for agent state, FeatureWorkflow for repo state
- **Visual**: Must integrate cleanly with existing project tree rendering

## Files to Create/Modify
- /home/owner/code/personal/git-frontend/internal/app/views/project.go (UPDATE) - Enhance renderTreeNode with workflow indicators, add workflow status panel rendering, add StreamTickMsg handling for live refresh

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Repo rows show inline workflow indicators (worktree, agent, push, MR) when workflow is active
- [ ] Agent status icons cycle correctly: running (●), complete (✓), error (✗)
- [ ] Workflow status panel shows branch name, state, and aggregate counts
- [ ] Panel shows per-repo detail with worktree, agent (with elapsed/cost), push, and MR status
- [ ] Panel uses box-drawing characters for visual borders
- [ ] Live auto-refresh (1s tick) updates agent status while agents are running
- [ ] Auto-refresh stops when no agents are running (no unnecessary ticking)
- [ ] Panel height is correctly calculated and filter height adjusted accordingly
- [ ] Theme styles are used consistently for status colors
- [ ] No full repo refresh on tick -- only workflow panel data updates
